newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end on downtrend amid Brazil woes.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end on downtrend amid Brazil woes.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished on a downtrend Tuesday as the market reversed earlier gains on concerns Brazil's buyback deal may not come out as well as hoped.
"There was some talk the Brazil deal was not going that well," said a trader at a foreign bank.
Argentine Brady bonds saw the brunt of the declines that set in late in the session while local bonds kept most gains.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was down 1/2 at 93 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was up $0.01 at 123.61.
Brazil's debt swap deal allowed investors to tender their par, discount and C bonds for a 30-year global bond issue. The offer expired Tuesday at 1900 GMT and results are expected Wednesday.
Another trader suggested the Argentine market saw profit-taking Tuesday after the rally in previous sessions.
Rumors that Argentina was planning a similar debt swap to Brazil were denied by an Economy Ministry official.
In the money markets, call money rates were flat at 5.78 percent.
